messages:
oliver: Heads-up — I opened a TF PR to move our legacy Ingress -> Gateway API behind ALB for customer-facing inference. Main change: ALB terminates TLS and re-encrypts to backend on 8443. Quick QA: can ALB do mTLS to the backend or do we need NLB passthrough? Also need advice on secretbinding for certs in a different namespace. PR: https://git.company/repo/pull/4821

maria: fyi this is when healthchecks start failing if backend-protocol isn't right. ALB supports HTTPS (re-encrypt) but not mTLS AFAIK. :thinking:

jess: correct — ALB can do HTTPS to the target (TLS re-encrypt) and validate server cert if you use target group TLS+server-name, but ALB cannot present a client cert to the backend for mTLS. If you need client cert auth to pods you need NLB passthrough or a sidecar that terminates+mutual-auths.

samir: quick checklist from infra: 1) set annotation for backend-protocol to HTTPS 2) health check protocol should be TCP or HTTPS depending on probe 3) ensure target group uses port 8443 and health path if HTTPS 4) secretbinding to namespace that the Gateway lives in

oliver: thx. any example annotations I can drop into TF?

jess: paste sample we use: ```yaml annotations:\n  alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/backend-protocol: "HTTPS"\n  alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/healthcheck-protocol: "HTTPS"\n  alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/target-group-attributes: "stickiness.enabled=true,slow_start.duration_seconds=30"\n```

maria: note — if you change to HTTPS healthcheck, pods must serve cert on health path or ALB health will mark unhealthy. Many of our inference pods only respond on plaintext probe port 8080. You can instead set healthcheck to TCP on port 8443 to avoid needing an HTTP path cert.

samir: on secretbinding: Gateway API secretbinding requires the secret to be in the same namespace as the gateway or use a SecretBinding resource (our cluster has the AWS Load Balancer Controller secretbinding CRD). For TF we create a k8s_secret in kops namespace and create an aws-alb-ingress-controller SecretBinding referencing it. If Gateway is in infra namespace but backend app in prod namespace, put the cert secret in infra (gateway) namespace and reference that from the Gateway class.

oliver: ok — so options: a) keep ALB HTTPS re-encrypt (no mTLS), put server certs on pods and trust ALB, b) switch to NLB passthrough if we really need client certs, c) insert a small TLS-terminating sidecar that performs mTLS to backend pods and accepts re-encrypted traffic from ALB. Which do we prefer?

jess: for low-latency inference, NLB passthrough is simplest for true mTLS; but you lose ALB L7 features (path routing, host header). If you need path-based routing and ALB features, do ALB -> sidecar mTLS. Depends on traffic shape.

maria: also consider cert rotation: if pods rotate server certs frequently, ALB TLS health + server name validation may fail. We usually pin to a CA bundle or disable server validation on ALB target group (less ideal). If you need strict validation, keep certs long-lived and use cert-manager to rotate with controlled overlap.

oliver: noted. One more: external-dns changes? TF added a CNAME + gateway hostname. Anyone for a quick review on the DNS snippet before I merge?

samir: I'll look in 20m. Also add a TF var to toggle use_nlb_passthrough so we can experiment in staging without big TF diffs later.

deploy-bot: PR pipeline started — plan in progress (job/terraform-plan #4821).

jess: small nit: healthcheck path for HTTPS target groups needs to be set like `"/healthz"` and `success_codes: "200"` in TF, otherwise ALB may treat 403/401 from mTLS-enforced endpoints as unhealthy. If you expect 401 for unauth'd probe, use TCP healthcheck.

oliver: sweet. I'll update PR: switch healthcheck -> TCP for staging, add use_nlb_passthrough var, and add secretbinding to infra ns. Thanks all. :raised_hands: 

infra-bot: Reminder: if you create Secret in infra namespace, ensure RBAC allows the load-balancer controller SA to read it: `kubectl create rolebinding alb-secret-reader --clusterrole=view --serviceaccount=infra:alb-controller -n infra`.
